policies.description: Only a user with the Administrator role may update a Service Offering, because only Administrator has Full CRUD access across all tables; Agent and Manager roles do not have CRUD rights for Service Offerings.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.

Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution.
Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables.

policies.description: Any request to update a Service Offering must include all mandatory fields; the tool requires the `service_offering_id` field, and at least one other field to change.
references: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: Do not assume the existence of a Service Offering ID; the ID must be verified via a lookup before calling the update operation.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.

policies.description: Perform only one validated update operation at a time; do not proceed if required data is missing or the current record state prevents the action.
references: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.

policies.policy_name: User Clarification on Missing Mandatory Fields
policies.description: If a mandatory field (e.g., `service_offering_id`) is missing from the request, the assistant must state which field is required instead of asking for more information.
references: If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.

policies.description: If the update request violates any policy (e.g., insufficient role, missing mandatory field), the assistant must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.
references: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.
